items.body: Free three-day event will feature watch parties, appearances from alumni, Stanley Cup HELSINKI – The 2026 NHL Global Series Fan Fest is coming to Helsinki. A first-class experience for fans of all ages, the free, three-day public event will bring the excitement of hockey to the heart of Helsinki, with more than 25 interactive activities and fan experiences, including hockey challenges, games, competitions and trivia; mascot and Stanley Cup appearances; and viewing parties for both 2026 NHL Global Series Finland regular-season games between the Carolina Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken on Nov. 12 at 7 p.m. and Nov. 14 at 8 p.m. (all times local). Located in Narinkkatori, the NHL Global Series Fan Fest will transform one of Helsinki’s most prominent public squares into a celebration of hockey for fans of all ages, from hands-on activities and school-group sessions to alumni appearances and the chance to see the Stanley Cup, the oldest and most revered trophy in professional sports. The 2026 NHL Global Series Fan Fest (formerly the NHL Global Fan Tour) will embark on its seventh season. Over the first six years, the touring event travelled to eight countries, visited 40 cities and has celebrated hockey with more than 440,000 fans. For the latest information on NHL Global Series Fan Fest , follow @nhlsuomi on Instagram and @NHL\_fi on X, or visit NHL.com/FanFest . items.title: Canucks battle to the end in combative loss to Ducks
items.summary: It was another game in which the rebuilding Canucks, even with their many flaws, were fully engaged, combative and played their opponents even at five-on-five.
items.body: VANCOUVER — Asked about the opportunity he is getting with the Vancouver Canucks , Jacob Quillan said: “This is everything.” A scoring star in college, the 24-year-old showed Tuesday night he is willing to do anything to stay in the National Hockey League by delivering the hit of the game and then fighting twice as the Canucks lost 5-4 to the Anaheim Ducks at Rogers Arena. Quillan did fine in his first two NHL fights when challenged by six-foot-five Roger McQueen, then rugged defenceman Travis Mitchell. He can’t build his career on fighting. But his willingness to stand up for himself — to show his new Canuck teammates he will fight for them — was notable on a night when Vancouver couldn’t survive its penalty killing or Ducks sniper Cutter Gauthier, but literally and figuratively battled their way back into the game against one of the league’s biggest teams. It was another game in which the rebuilding Canucks, even with their many flaws, were fully engaged, combative and played their opponents even at five-on-five. Down three goals in the third period, the Canucks surged back with a pair of goals from Jake DeBrusk and generated significant offensive-zone pressure at the end. Jonathan Lekkerimaki just missed on a couple of shot-pass redirects from the high slot as Vancouver attacked six-against-five before losing for the 13 th time in 14 games. Their only win during this spiral came a week ago when the Canucks stunned the Ducks in Anaheim by rallying from a three-goal deficit to win 6-5 in overtime, which probably partly explains the feistiness of the rematch. items.title: Canadiens on wrong side of history in skid-stopping comeback win for Jets
items.summary: No matter how poorly the Canadiens played, they were in the best position possible with the clock ticking down, and then they inexcusably crumbled.
items.body: MONTREAL — This was a bad game from start to finish for the Montreal Canadiens , but to suggest it ended the way it should’ve — with the Winnipeg Jets making NHL history to avoid a 10th straight loss — would be bending the truth. For the Canadiens had a 4-0 lead with 2:40 to play, and when Cole Caufield , who scored two of their goals, said it should’ve ended well before they lost in overtime, he was right. No matter how poorly his team played, it was in the best position it could possibly be in with the clock ticking down, and then it inexcusably crumbled. Four Jets goals in 2:39, and one more from Dylan Samberg with 1:30 to go in overtime, sealed the Canadiens’ fate. Afterwards, Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis said, “We got smacked in the teeth and maybe that’s what we needed as a team,” and he was also probably right. If you look at all five games the Canadiens won in succession without Nick Suzuki before this one, a couple of them — including the one at the Heritage Classic in Winnipeg — were hand-delivered by Jacob Fowler . Having one more gifted to them by the rookie goaltender, who stopped the first 36 Jets shots he faced Tuesday, might’ve only reinforced some bad habits that had slowly crept into their play. “We definitely felt like there were certain games where we could be playing better,” said Kaiden Guhle . “We were finding ways to win, and just tonight it bit us and it caught up to us.” If it brings the Canadiens back down to earth a bit and gets them to reinvest in the good habits that had been so prevalent through the nine games before Suzuki went down, it’ll serve its purpose. items.title: Oilers continue to look like different team despite loss to speedy Devils
items.summary: Life isn’t so bad for the last team in the NHL without a regulation road loss. Mark Spector has more on the new-look Oilers from New Jersey.
items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Eight good periods out of nine. Two wins in three games. Five points out of a possible six. If this is as bad as it gets for the Edmonton Oilers — getting buckled in the second period of a 4-3 shootout loss against the fast and furious New Jersey Devils — then life can’t be so bad for the last team in the National Hockey League without a regulation loss on the road (7-0-1). As the Oilers fly home from their annual New York roadie, they continue to look like an entirely different team under head coach Mike Babcock. With a four-game homestand beginning Thursday, Edmonton has never-before-seen structure, excellent goaltending, and an 11-2-3 record that’s good for second place in the NHL’s overall standings. “The details of what we are, and what we're about, are there. The work ethic — the expectation to be heavy and physical and be fast — are there,” assessed third-line centre Jason Dickinson. “Sometimes the execution is missing in puck play and decision making, and that's probably where we could really tidy things up.” On this night the power play returned with two goals, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins had 1-1-2 on the night he became the all-time longest serving Oiler (1,038 games), and Tristan Jarry authored a point-saving performance, stopping 31 shots in his best game of the season. items.title: Maple Leafs lose momentum after Raddysh penalty in loss to Mammoth
items.body: TORONTO — It seemed like a night in need of a marathon effort. For two periods of this Tuesday night tilt under the Scotiabank Arena lights, the Toronto Maple Leafs looked out of step, out of sorts. The visiting Utah Mammoth had them on their heels — the hosts were down 2-1 after 40 minutes and netminder Sergei Bobrovsky was peppered to the tune of 30 shots, nearly double what the man on the other side of the sheet had weathered. But slowly, steadily, the home side started to find their game, piecing together some promising sequences, pushing back against a Utah side that had wobbled them once already, three weeks ago in Salt Lake City. By the midway point of the third period, the Maple Leafs had navigated a path back to even ground when Jack Roslovic netted his second of the night to pull his squad back into the fight. The ice was tilting. The crowd was buzzing. With less than half a period left to play, Barrett Hayton drew Darren Raddysh into a back-and-forth to the right of the Maple Leafs' cage. The blue-liner tagged Hayton with a cross-check to the back, then another as the Utah forward turned to face him. Hayton then clamped down on Raddysh’s stick, and the pair of them fell to the ice. But the veteran defender dug in, raining another stiff cross-check down on the centreman as he lay on the ice. A minute-and-a-half later, the puck was sitting in the Maple Leafs' net, the game-winner coming off Nick Schmaltz’s stick on the Mammoth's second power-play dagger of the tilt. items.body: Long-time executive had gruff exterior but legacy is being 'a truly good human being' The 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 9. This year's class includes Carey Price , Pekka Rinne , Patrice Bergeron , Keith Tkachuk and Cindy Curley in the Player category and Brian Burke in the Builder category. Here, NHL.com senior writer Tracey Myers profiles Burke. Brian Burke was 12 years old when his life trajectory unknowingly was set during a family move from Boston to Minnesota. “The moving trucks got stuck in a blizzard in Pennsylvania with all our furniture and stuff, so we were stuck in a hotel for three nights in Bloomington, Minnesota,” Burke said. “The state high-school hockey tournament was on. That’s when I fell in love with the game, watching high-school hockey.” That love affair has lasted Burke’s entire life, and the 71-year-old has been one of the most impactful people in so many areas of hockey. "When I think of his image, the thing that first pops into my head, he used to have a picture in his office at the League of him on the ice in a Maine Mariners uniform with blood all over his face," NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman said. "That's one image that he gives off, but the other image is somebody who's concerned about people, embraces people and relationships, and if you're his friend, he'll go to all ends of the Earth to support you and be there for you, which is the mark of a truly good human being." Burke's NHL career began in 1987 when he was named vice president and director of hockey operations for the Vancouver Canucks. Then In 1992, he became general manager of the Hartford Whalers. items.body: NHL Commissioner writes special testimonial for friend, colleague A few months after Gary Bettman was named the first Commissioner in NHL History on Feb. 1, 1993, he hired Brian Burke to be the League’s senior vice president and director of hockey operations. Burke served as the League’s chief disciplinarian, and he oversaw the on-ice officials. He also worked with Bettman on League direction and collective bargaining matters. Burke left his League job in 1998 to become president and general manager of the Vancouver Canucks, but he remains a great friend of Bettman, who Burke considers one of his mentors. With Burke being inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday as a Builder, Bettman, in a special testimonial for NHL.com, writes about his working and personal relationship with Burke and his impact on the game. There are few people who have had such a diverse career in the game and there are few people who have been as committed to the game both on and off the ice as Brian Burke. In addition to all the work he’s done either as a player or an agent or an executive at the club level or League level, he’s always been a part of giving back, using the game as a platform to be involved in the community. This week spotlights a unique New York Rangers broadcaster whose other life happens to be as chief operating officer of a thriving Brooklyn beverage company. There are not enough hours in a 24-hour day for Dave Starman, but somehow he makes do with his dream job and family business. Between his role as radio analyst of the New York Rangers and chief operating officer of the Autotap Corporation, Starman, 58, is busier than a paperhanger with an itch. "I adore every minute of it," Starman said in an email, "and I never get tired because I love both my jobs." Autotap is service provider of fountain beverage services started by Starman's great grandfather, Joseph, in 1900 and incorporated in 1925. "My job is to supervise sales, service and installation of fountain beverage equipment, soda, beer and wine systems," Starman said. "I also keep track of 10 trucks handling delivery routes throughout the city." And without taking a deep breath, Starman personally answers every customer email "because we care about them." Yeah, it keeps him busy, but not too busy for hockey, his lifetime love. A passionate affection for the Rangers, and being a goalie, has been part of Starman's life since he was knee-high to a grasshopper, growing up in Belle Harbor, New York, on the Rockaway Peninsula in Queens. "I played goal for the Greater New York Stars and later the University of Hartford," he said, "and drifted into coaching with a youth hockey team in Connecticut. items.title: Jets pull record latest four-goal comeback in NHL history to end drought
items.summary: The Jets had lost nine straight games prior to the shocking late-game effort.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources If any Winnipeg Jets fans left the Bell Centre early to beat the traffic, you’re in for a rude awakening. The Jets failed to score through 57:21 against the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday. But after Tyrel Bauer scored his first career goal, everything changed. The Jets ended up scoring three more goals to complete the latest four-goal comeback victory in NHL history. The previous record was set on Nov. 10, 2007, when the Los Angeles Kings scored four goals against Dallas after the 52:46 mark. According to the NHL, this is just the fourth time this has occured after the 50:00 mark, and just the first to have it happen in the final five minutes of a game. Montreal looked in full control, with Owen Beck, Josh Anderson, Cole Caufield (twice) finding the back of the net. Bauer’s goal put an end to Jacob Fowler’s shutout effort, and, seemingly, that felt like the only thing the Jets could get excited about. Instead, Morgan Barron scored less than a minute later, and Kyle Connor made it a one-goal game at 19:00. Just 27 seconds later, Connor recorded his second of the night and 13th of the season, sending the game in overtime after the Jets scored four goals in 2:39 of regulation. Winnipeg wouldn’t stop there. At 3:30 in overtime, Dylan Samberg’s snap shot would beat Fowler to give the Jets the stunning overtime victory, ending the team’s nine-game losing streak in the process. Their last win came on October 13, a 5-2 victory over Minnesota. The Jets finished the game with a 47-22 shot advantage. Notably, this was Montreal’s first game with the club’s new Hometown Remix jersey. The Jets will look to keep the momentum alive on Nov. 5 when the team hosts the Vancouver Canucks.

items.title: Lowe congratulates Nugent-Hopkins on games played record
items.summary:
Kevin Lowe was happy to see his record broken by Ryan Nugent-Hopkins.
The Hockey Hall of Famer congratulated the Edmonton Oilers forward on playing his 1,038th game with the team, passing Lowe on the franchise’s games played list, in a video posted by Sportsnet on Tuesday.
items.body: Kevin Lowe was happy to see his record broken by Ryan Nugent-Hopkins . The Hockey Hall of Famer congratulated the Edmonton Oilers forward on playing his 1,038 th game with the team, passing Lowe on the franchise’s games played list, in a video posted by Sportsnet on Tuesday. Kevin Lowe with a message to Ryan Nugent-Hopkins 🧡💙 pic.twitter.com/Ns6f2HKICI “Ryan, Congratulations on becoming the all-time leader in regular seasons game played as an Edmonton Oiler,” Lowe said in the video message. “That record has stood around for 28 years and I’ve been extremely proud of it. “But as we all know, records are meant to be broken. So, if someone is going to take it away from me, I couldn’t think of a more popular Oiler to do it.” The six-time Stanley Cup winner played 15 of his 19 NHL seasons with the Oilers, amounting to 1,037 games. Before the Oilers game against the New Jersey Devils, the team celebrated Nugent-Hopkins’ record with custom T-shirts as they arrived at Prudential Center. In the second period, Nugent-Hopkins netted a power play goal to mark his milestone game. He also recorded an assist on defenseman Evan Bouchard ’s first period goal. Nugent-Hopkins is in his 16 th season with the Oilers, who drafted him with the No. 1 pick in the 2011 NHL Draft. He has 295 goals and 518 assists in his 1,038 games with the team.

items.title: Oilers fall to Hellebuyck, Devils in shootout
items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Jack Hughes scored two goals and had an assist, Connor Hellebuyck made 19 saves to win his first home start of the season, and the New Jersey Devils halted the Edmonton Oilers ' winning streak at three with a 4-3 shootout decision on Tuesday night. Fans chanted “USA! USA!” after Hughes' first goal, a nod to him scoring the winner in overtime to deliver gold for the U.S. at the Olympics against Canada in the final. Hellebuyck, who backstopped the Americans in Milan, was making his third start for the Devils since they traded for him. Arseny Gritsyuk got the shootout winner and Connor Brown also scored in regulation against the Oilers, who he played with for two seasons and helped reach the Stanley Cup Final in 2024 and '25. The Devils have won two in a row and five of their past six. Connor McDavid extended his NHL record season-opening assist streak to 16 games with his league-leading 31st. Evan Bouchard, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Leon Draisaitl scored for Edmonton, and Tristan Jarry had his shutout streak ended after more than seven periods without allowing a goal but finished with 31 saves. Skating in his 1,038th regular season game, Nugent-Hopkins broke a tie with Hall of Famer Kevin Lowe for the most in Oilers franchise history. Players wore T-shirts with that number and a caricature of Nugent-Hopkins on it. Edmonton was without fellow forward Isaac Howard, who coach Mike Babcock said will miss a couple of weeks with a left knee injury that is not considered a long-term issue. Forward Trent Frederic was a healthy scratch, while defenceman Jake Walman returned after missing the past three. Oilers: Open a four-game homestand Thursday against the Anaheim Ducks.

items.body: Register Login Miro Heiskanen Exits Game With Upper-Body Injury By Ryan Long | at November 3, 2026 9:17 pm Stars defenseman Miro Heiskanen left and did not return to tonight’s game against the Capitals due to an upper-body injury, the team announced. Heiskanen exited after his first shift of the second period, during which he took a hit from Capitals forward Justin Sourdif . While the severity of the injury remains to be seen, any absence would be a significant loss for Dallas’ blue line. The 27-year-old entered tonight with three goals and 11 points in 14 games while averaging 25:58 of ice time. He continues to anchor the Stars’ top pairing alongside fellow Finn Esa Lindell . The two logged roughly 1,022 minutes together last season, the seventh-most of any defense pair in the league. Heiskanen is also central to both of Dallas’ special teams units. Last season, he was the only player in the NHL to average more than three minutes per game on both the power play (3:27) and the penalty kill (3:06). Those minutes came in a strong bounce-back year. After a knee injury and surgery cost him most of the 2024-25 campaign, Heiskanen posted 63 points (nine goals, 54 assists) in 77 games last season. He ranked ninth among NHL defensemen in scoring and fourth among all players in average ice time at 25:28, and he set a career high with 132 blocked shots. He also helped Finland win bronze at the 2026 Winter Olympics with five points in six games and led all Olympic skaters in average ice time. The third overall pick in 2017 entered tonight with 357 career points in 566 games and is 13 assists shy of 300. items.body: TAMPA, Fla. — Brayden Point scored two goals, Anthony Cirelli got one and the Tampa Bay Lightning beat the Detroit Red Wings 4-2 on Tuesday night for their seventh straight home win. Reigning NHL MVP Nikita Kucherov had two assists in his first home game since asking the Lightning for a trade, and goalie Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 19 shots. Lucas Raymond and J.T. Compher scored Detroit’s goals. The Red Wings pulled their goalie for an extra shooter for the final three minutes and put plenty of pressure on Vasilevskiy but couldn't get the tying goal. Ryan McDonagh slid an empty-netter down the ice with 1 second left. Point gave the Lightning 1-0 lead with a power-play goal in the first period. He didn’t quite get everything on his shot in the low slot off Kucherov’s centering pass but it went past goalie John Gibson. Point snapped a shot over Gibson’s glove 5:07 later to make it 2-0. Kucherov set it up with another perfect pass. Gibson was replaced by Daniil Tarasov to start the second period after stopping 11 of 13 shots in the first. Cirelli lifted his fifth goal past Tarasov into the top left corner for a 3-0 lead in the second period. Raymond fired a shot from the left point past Vasilevskiy midway through the second to cut it to 3-1. The Red Wings got within 3-2 less than six minutes into the third when Compher scored a power-play goal, blasting a shot from the right circle underneath Vasilevskiy’s left pad. Kucherov has five assists in two games since informing the team he wants to be traded. Kucherov said Monday he made the request because he feels disrespected by a lack of communication with general manager Julien BriseBois. items.body: Register Login John Gibson Exits Game With Lower-Body Injury By Ryan Long | at November 3, 2026 8:04 pm Red Wings goaltender John Gibson left tonight’s game against the Lightning with a lower-body injury and will not return, the team announced . Gibson allowed two goals on 11 shots while playing the entire first period, and it isn’t exactly clear when he was hurt. If he misses more time, Daniil Tarasov would take over as Detroit’s starter and the Red Wings would need to recall a goaltender from AHL Grand Rapids to fill out the roster. This is the second time in less than two weeks that Gibson has left a game early. He sat out the third period of Detroit’s 5-2 win over the Canucks on October 22 with what the team called an upper-body injury, but he was back in net two days later in Calgary. The 33-year-old has struggled early this season. Gibson came into tonight 4-5-1 with a 3.37 GAA and an .860 save percentage in 10 appearances. That’s a sharp drop from his first season in Detroit, when he went 29-22-4 with a 2.72 GAA and a .901 save percentage in 57 games, his heaviest workload since 2018-19. He is in the final year of his contract, which carries a $6.4MM cap hit. Tarasov has been strong in limited work since signing a one-year, $2MM deal with Detroit in free agency on July 1. In his first start with the club, the 27-year-old stopped all 30 shots he faced in regulation and overtime in a 1-0 shootout loss in Montreal. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images As if Hockeytown needs even more bad news. As the second period between the Detroit Red Wings and Tampa Bay Lightning began Tuesday night, Red Wings goaltender John Gibson didn’t take the ice. The team later announced that Gibson wouldn’t return to the contest due to a lower-body injury. Gibson gave up two goals on 13 shots in the opening 20 minutes, as the Red Wings found themselves trailing 2-0 heading into the first intermission. Daniil Tarasov entered the game in relief, less than 24 hours after earning the win against his former team, the Florida Panthers . This is far from the first time Gibson has been hurt in his NHL career, and it isn’t the first time he’s had to prematurely leave a game this season. Back on Oct. 22, he suffered an upper-body injury in a game against the Vancouver Canucks , but returned to the crease two nights later. While it’s too early to tell the severity of Gibson’s injury and how long he could be out of action, Detroit doesn’t have a whole lot of time to waste, as the team returns home on Thursday night to host the Vegas Golden Knights. If Gibson’s injury is more than a small tweak, expect Michal Postava to be called up from the Grand Rapids Griffins, the Red Wings’ American Hockey League affiliate. Postava picked up a win in his first NHL start last Monday and was just named the AHL’s goaltender of the month. Gibson has been Detroit’s No. 1 netminder since he came to the Original Six franchise in June 2025. However, he hasn’t nearly had as strong a start to this season as he did last year. In his first 10 starts, the 33-year-old is 4-5-1, with a 3.37 goals-against average and an .860 save percentage.

Wright, the No. 4 pick in the 2022 NHL Draft, has four points (three goals, one assist) in 14 games this season. The center played 167 games with the Kraken since the start of 2024-25 after playing the majority of the previous season with Coachella Valley of the American Hockey League. "I was surprised, but I was excited as well," Wright said Monday. "Really unbelievable city and organization. I'm excited to be here. "I think, for me, I always wanted a little more opportunity. I wanted to have more minutes. I wanted to play a bigger role, whether that was in Seattle or somewhere else. I was happy to do that, but I'm moving on from the situation and happy to be here. I'm still young, so I want to hopefully be here for a number of years, build something special here and be part of a winning culture and a winning group." The 22-year-old has 82 points (39 goals, 43 assists) in 183 NHL games. Wright had nine points (two goals, seven assists) in 24 AHL playoff games in 2023, helping Coachella Valley reach the Calder Cup Finals before losing to Hershey. On Tuesday, the team unveiled a special Dolly Parton jersey patch that will be worn on sweaters during warmups before the team’s matchup against the St. Louis Blues on Saturday, Nov. 7 (1 p.m. ET; STLNHL, BN+, NHLN, SN+, SCRIPPS). items.title: Flames legend Jarome Iginla battling health issues
items.summary: Jarome Iginla is facing a battle far removed from the rink. Eric Francis spoke to the Flames legend about the health issues he’s dealing with.
items.body: CALGARY - For years, Jarome Iginla played through just about everything hockey could throw at him. Broken bones, bruises, bumps, slashes, playoff wars and the relentless punishment of more than 1,600 NHL games. Nothing seemed capable of keeping one of the toughest competitors in Calgary Flames history down for long. Now, the Hockey Hall of Famer is facing a battle far removed from the rink. “Unfortunately I have been battling some health issues,” said the 49-year-old from his home in Lake Country, B.C. “Some neurological issues. I’m not entirely sure what it is, it may be from metal toxins from reaction to the cobalt hip.” Iginla underwent hip replacement surgery a few years ago after a career spent absorbing the physical toll of professional hockey. Complications followed, along with medications that have affected his energy, weight and speech. There are concerns that the cobalt-chromium components used in some artificial hip implants can release metal ions and debris through wear or corrosion, potentially causing complications as they enter the bloodstream. He also had high mercury levels in his body and is working to get that down, while trying to determine if the cause is related to the cobalt poisoning. items.summary: Lambert has just one assist through 11 games this season, but could be utilized more in the AHL.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images A struggling center looks to be on his way back down to the minors, where a larger role awaits. On Tuesday, the Winnipeg Jets placed forward Brad Lambert on waivers, making him available to the other 31 teams in the NHL. If Lambert clears waivers on Wednesday, he’ll become eligible to be assigned to the Jets’ American Hockey League affiliate, the Manitoba Moose. Lambert has been in the lineup for most of the first month of the 2026-27 season in Winnipeg, but, like the team around him, hasn’t done much. In 11 appearances, he has just one assist, that coming in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Chicago Blackhawks on Oct. 15. He has gone pointless in each of his previous five games, last dressing in the Jets lineup last Thursday, when the team lost a tough battle to the Tampa Bay Lightning , 5-4. The 22-year-old logged less than nine minutes of ice time in the defeat. Lambert has a plus/minus of -5 while averaging 9:10 of ice time per game. There was belief that Lambert could see some considerable playing time with the Jets this season. He posted three goals and six points in 25 contests during the 2025-26 season, the most during a single campaign in his brief NHL tenure. However, the organization appears to believe his talent could be used in the AHL. In 42 games in the NHL, the former first-round pick has three goals and nine points. In 173 regular-season games in the AHL, Lambert has posted 36 goals and 70 assists for 106 points, with one assist in nine Calder Cup Playoff contests. The only player put on waivers on Monday was Toronto Maple Leafs forward Bo Groulx. He cleared and can now be sent down to the Leafs’ top farm team, the Toronto Marlies.

But the Canadian defenceman says Russia's return to international competition might be viewed differently by European players. "I know those (Russian) guys want to play in it really badly, but it's obviously a different time, and people have their views on it," Weegar said Tuesday before his Utah Mammoth played the Maple Leafs in Toronto. " But I've always loved seeing Russia in the Olympics and in those best-on-bests." The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled last week that the International Ice Hockey Federation must reinstate Russian teams, beginning with the world juniors, which start Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. Russia and its ally Belarus had been barred from competition since Russia began its invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The ruling has prompted a backlash from several European hockey federations. Sweden, Finland, Czechia and Latvia have said their national teams will not play Russia in international competition. Norway and Denmark have said they will not play Russia at the 2027 men’s world championship in Germany, while Austria opposes Russia’s return. "It's different for those countries out there, right? items.title: Oilers’ Howard out week-to-week with lower-body injury
items.summary: Howard was hurt when he was on the wrong end of a knee-on-knee hit from the Islanders’ Emil Heineman.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Peter Creveling-Imagn Images A young up-and-comer is going to miss an extended period of time. When speaking to the media on Tuesday, Edmonton Oilers head coach Mike Babcock revealed that forward Isaac Howard is considered week-to-week with a lower-body injury. Babcock noted that Howard is doing better and seems optimistic that he’ll return sooner rather than later. “[Howard] is good,” Babcock said. “He’s going to be out a couple weeks, I think. But it’s nothing. It’s not a big deal.” Howard was hurt during Saturday night’s game between the Oilers and the New York Islanders . Early in the first period, Islanders forward Emil Heineman delivered a knee-on-knee hit to Howard in the neutral zone. Howard needed assistance getting off the ice. He returned to the Edmonton locker room and was later ruled out for the rest of the game, logging just 30 seconds of ice time. Heineman was given a five-minute major penalty for kneeing and a game misconduct. For Howard, who has played in all but two games for the Oilers so far this season, he will miss at least the remainder of the team’s road trip out East, which concludes on Tuesday night against the New Jersey Devils . Edmonton returns home on Thursday, taking on the Anaheim Duck s, beginning a four-game homestand. In just his second season with the Oilers, the 2025 Hobey Baker winner has produced a little bit on the offensive end. In 13 contests, he has scored a goal and three points, just a couple off matching his five-point performance from last season, where he dressed in 29 games. items.title: Checking in on early returns of Maple Leafs’ go-to goalie Sergei Bobrovsky
items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs’ decision to sign Sergei Bobrovsky for three years came with enormous risk. Has it been worth it? Adam Vingan checks in on the early returns.
items.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs ’ decision to sign Sergei Bobrovsky for three years came with enormous risk. General manager John Chayka gambled that a goaltender — albeit one destined for the Hockey Hall of Fame — coming off the worst season of his career at 37 would rebound. At least to start the season, the worst-case scenario has come to pass. Sure, it’s a small sample size, but Bobrovsky has allowed at least three goals in nine of his 10 starts, already leading to questions about whether the Maple Leafs should adjust his workload. “We brought (Bobrovsky) in to be there when the pressure ramps up and we need a rock back there,” Chayka told reporters . Unfortunately, Bobrovsky has yet to harden into that rock. His .809 save percentage on slot shots ranks 39th out of 53 goaltenders who have appeared in at least five games this season. It is an improvement from the .789 he posted last season with the Florida Panthers that ranked 64th among 66 qualified goaltenders (minimum 20 games played). But more is expected from the ninth-highest-paid goaltender in that group. (Across Florida’s consecutive Stanley Cup-winning seasons in 2023-24 and 2024-25, Bobrovsky recorded an .839 slot save percentage.) “I don’t try to overthink, I try to stay just with the moment and try to stop the next shot,” Bobrovsky told reporters . “It is a new team. It’s not only me, lots of new pieces, new system, new guys, so we just build the chemistry, build the belief.” All athletes, even those as finely tuned as Bobrovsky, eventually lose their sharpness. In Bobrovsky’s case, his reflexes appear to have slowed. Opponents have been picking on Bobrovsky’s glove hand, which seems to have lost some of its zip. items.body: Register Login Matthew Poitras Suffered Face Injury By Marcus Antonelli | at November 3, 2026 10:43 am Matthew Poitras is not present at Bruins practice, according to Scott McLaughlin of WEEI . The reasoning behind that regards a hit he sustained in the Bruins’ 3-2 shootout win over the reigning Western Conference Champion Vegas Golden Knights. Poitras, while carrying the puck through the neutral zone, funneled a cross-ice pass as he skated near the benches. Braeden Bowman , who was parallel to the young center, made contact with his head, using his elbow to knock down Poitras at 2:49 of the second period. Poitras was able to will himself off the ice and returned with a full bubble shield, but did not play another shift. Poitras ended his night with 3:13 of ice time. Sean Kuraly skated on the fourth line at Bruins practice. Marco Sturm did not provide a postgame update. Bowman received a five-minute major and a game misconduct. According to Frank Seravalli , Bowman has not received any more discipline. As he described it, Bowman made sure his elbow was close to his body; as a result, this is not viewed as elbowing, per Seravalli. Along with the reverse angle showing Poitras skating into Bowman, his head is not ‘deemed to be the principal point of contact.’ Poitras has been a key player for the Bruins this season. The 22-year-old, who has 7 points in 12 NHL games, has gotten more leeway compared to his past two years under the organization, which saw much more time in the AHL with the Providence Bruins. Playing fourth-line minutes at that scoring clip, Poitras has been a major part of the Bruins’ youth movement. He’s within the top-10 scorers on Boston, and is 10th in the entire NHL in scoring per 60 minutes, with 3.78, just playing under 10 minutes of average ice time.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources A new wrinkle in the saga following an international court’s controversial decision. After a cabinet meeting on Monday, Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis announced that the country will not issue visas to Russian players seeking to compete in the upcoming IIHF Under-18 Women’s World Championship, set to take place in Ostrava from Jan. 8-16. Babis cited the ongoing war in Ukraine as a major reason the country wouldn’t allow Russia to play in the event. “It doesn’t make sense to me as long as the war in Ukraine continues,” Babis said in his translated remarks. “It would create the impression that war and killing are normal, which we reject.” The announcement comes after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on Friday that the Russian Ice Hockey Federation can immediately participate in International Ice Hockey Federation tournaments, ending a ban instituted after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Babis added that he believes in the separation of politics and athletics, but the CAS’ decision waives that notion. “I agree that politics should not interfere with sports, but this decision brings politics into it.” In 2023, Czechia instituted a suspension of granting visas to Russian national teams. items.body: Hockey Hall of Famer, New Jersey exec thrilled to land goalie in trade with Jets Martin Brodeur believed the New Jersey Devils reached the point where a move for an elite goaltender like Connor Hellebuyck wasn't just warranted. It was necessary. New Jersey's core players are entering or firmly established in the prime of their careers. Brodeur, its executive vice president of hockey operations, said acquiring the 33-year-old goalie reflects the Devils' commitment to take the next step. "It's like the window of winning," Brodeur said in an interview with NHL Network on Tuesday. "Our guys are there. You look at Nico Hischier (27 years old), Jack Hughes (25), Jesper Bratt (28), Timo Meier (30), they're (mostly) all in their late 20s, with Jack a little younger. But I think it was time for us to make a move like that. (General manager) Sunny (Mehta) pulled it off, and it's awesome." Brodeur understands perhaps better than anyone what Hellebuyck provides -- a proven No. 1 goalie who embraces the responsibility that comes with being one of the most important players on the team. Hellebuyck made 17 saves Tuesday for his first victory with New Jersey, a 5-1 win at the Dallas Stars in his first NHL game since April 13, four days after being acquired in a trade with the Winnipeg Jets for forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad , goalie Nico Daws , the rights to unsigned draft choice Alexander Command , the Devils' own second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft and their seventh-round selection in the 2027 NHL Draft. Brodeur played 1,266 games during his 22-season NHL career, including 1,259 with New Jersey, and won the Vezina Trophy as the League's best goalie four times (2003, 2004, 2007, 2008) and the Stanley Cup three times (1995, 2000, 2003). items.title: Takeaways: Wolf continues return to form as Flames beat Sharks
items.summary: Devin Cooley’s mid-heater injury gave Dustin Wolf a chance to regain his past form. He made good on the opportunity Monday night in San Jose, writes Eric Francis.
items.body: Minutes after Dustin Wolf came in in relief for his first appearance in two weeks, Ryan Huska was asked if his goaltender’s chief goal was to build confidence. “That’s all it is — get his back up a little bit and just go play. He’s a really good goaltender. He gives us a chance to win every time he’s in the net.” With Devin Cooley’s five-game heater stopped by an injury that is expected to keep him out week-to-week, Wolf is already making good on his chance to return to form. Wolf won his second consecutive start Monday in San Jose, stopping 26 of 27 shots in a 2-1 win at a SAP Center rink he’s intimately familiar with. He’s now 11-2 against the Sharks, which includes going 5-1 in the rink in which his family had season tickets when he was a kid. “I’ve got a lot of memories in this building as a fan, growing up watching the Sharks for a long time,” said the native of nearby Gilroy, Calif., who had his grandmother, cousins and an aunt and uncle in attendance. “I didn’t have the start to the year, on a personal level, that I wanted. (Two weeks off) gave me a chance to kind of reset my mind and work on some parts of my game I wanted to get better at. I feel pretty confident in that now.” Wolf was particularly under siege in the final two minutes of the second period, when a Sharks power play had the Flames pinned in their zone for the entirety of Simon Nemec’s too-many-men penalty. With the Flames up 2-0 in the third, Sam Dickinson beat Wolf through a crowd with eight minutes left, but Wolf held steady despite a late Sharks push. As the game’s first star, it’s safe to say he is rebuilding his confidence. items.body: Calls Nashville star 'the most respectful, humble person you could possibly meet' Ben Vanderklok first began working with Pekka Rinne in 2014, when he was hired to be the Nashville Predators goaltending coach. Rinne already was Nashville's long-established No. 1 goalie. One year apart in age, with Vanderklok approaching his 33rd birthday and Rinne his 32nd, a relationship was formed a dozen years ago that continues today. They worked together as goalie and goalie coach until Rinne's retirement following the 2020-21 season. Now they work together in the Predators' goaltending department, with Vanderklok still the goaltending coach and Rinne the club's European development coach and scout. They have become great friends and rely on each other's friendship and insight almost daily. As such, who better than Vanderklok, who will be on hand for Rinne's induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday, to give NHL.com readers an inside peek behind the scenes at what "Peks" is really like. My relationship with Pekka Rinne started my first year in the League. We're only a year apart in age and I remember not knowing what this is going to be like. I remember thinking, "Yeah, I'm excited to get my first NHL opportunity, but also it's Pekka Rinne and we're almost the same age." I remember having a couple of weeks wondering how this is going to be. But I also remember our first conversation and how engaged he was. Rinne's rise began with a reality check pep talk from Harri Hautamaki, his coach when he was a teenager growing up in Kempele, Finland, about 15 minutes from Oulu. "I played on a tiny little team called Kiekko-Laser; that's where Harri coached me," Rinne said. "I ended up having two really good years with Harri, but we basically played in a second-division Finnish junior program, so it was very local games. We didn't travel a lot." Hautamaki, as Rinne recalled, saw more in the goalie than the goalie saw in himself. In this edition, Kevin Dean, former assistant coach of the Boston Bruins, Chicago Blackhawks and Vancouver Canucks, discusses the importance of communication with players and developing an identity, in conjunction with implementing a system, is during the early part of the NHL season. Systems are important in hockey, particularly in the NHL. It’s the blueprint of how a team plays. But the reason a team plays the way it does is just as important. It is necessary to have a system and an investment in the players in equal measure. That’s what you see from good teams at any level. If a coach can get his players to play to the best of their ability, the chosen system will work better. If you can get 75 percent of your players at their best, you are going to probably have success. You're going to win. Look, I am a fan of the Milwaukee Brewers and what they just did was incredible in winning the World Series. That's not a high-end team talent-wise, but every player on that team was pretty much playing as well as you can play, right? That's the magic of a good coach. How do you get eight out of every 10 of your players to be at, or near, their best? Focusing on maximizing the individual can be successful. Hockey is the ultimate team sport, so why not maximize the team’s potential by maximizing the pieces within the team? items.body: Forward does not return after taking last shift at 14:53 of second period, expected to miss ‘couple of games’ CHICAGO -- Patrick Kane left in the second period with an upper-body injury and did not return for the Chicago Blackhawks in a 5-2 loss against the Colorado Avalanche at United Center on Monday. “We have to go see how he’s doing, see if he’s all right,” forward Frank Nazar said. “I don’t know what happened, if it was in this game, wish I saw it and done something. Obviously hope he’s all right.” Chicago coach Jeff Blashill said after the game that Kane is “going to miss the next couple of games, for sure." Kane has nine points (one goal, eight assists) in 15 games, second on the Blackhawks behind captain Connor Bedard with 10 points (four goals, six assists). His eight assists lead the Blackhawks. He’s averaging 18:02 of ice time this season, third among Blackhawks forwards behind Bedard (20:35) and Roman Kantserov (18:24). “It goes without saying, he’s one of the heartbeats of this team, the guy we lean on so much, on and off the ice,” Bedard said. “The biggest thing is we just hope he’s fine and hope he’s ready to go as soon as possible. The Court of Abritration for Sport ruled on Friday that the International Ice Hockey Federation was to allow Russia to participate in IIHF World Championship tournaments, starting with the 2027 World Junior Championship in Edmonton and Red Deer. Since then, various top-level countries have shared their disappointment in the decision. “We are currently gathering as many countries as possible to form a common front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia in this situation,” Finnish chairman Heikki Hietanen said in a translated statement. “This weighs significantly more heavily in the balance than the fact that we only announce the matter on our own behalf.” According to the statement, the Finnish Ice Hockey Association board said they plan to keep “all possible means at its disposal to resolve the matter.” The IIHF board of directors met on Monday as part of a two-day meeting to discuss the issue. “It is the IIHF’s responsibility to inform about the meeting once a decision has been made.
